name: Belimumab
route_note: IV infusion every 4 weeks after loading, or weekly subcutaneous injection
originator: Human Genome Sciences with Cambridge Antibody Technology

discovery.by: Human Genome Sciences and Cambridge Antibody Technology
discovery.note: Fully human IgG1λ antibody against soluble B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS/BAFF), isolated by phage display. Year of the first published characterisation of the antibody (as LymphoStat-B; Baker et al., Arthritis Rheum 2003).

tagline: First targeted biologic for lupus, blocking the B-cell survival factor BLyS
summary: Belimumab is a human monoclonal antibody that neutralises soluble B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS, also called BAFF). Approved in 2011, it was the first new drug for systemic lupus erythematosus in more than 50 years and is also used for lupus nephritis.
mechanism: BLyS is a TNF-family cytokine that binds BAFF-R, TACI and BCMA on B cells and promotes their survival and maturation; levels are raised in many patients with lupus.

Belimumab binds soluble BLyS and prevents receptor binding, causing apoptosis of autoreactive transitional and naïve B cells and lowering autoantibody levels, without directly depleting memory B cells or plasma cells.
uses: Active autoantibody-positive systemic lupus erythematosus (adults and children ≥5 years) on standard therapy

history.title: BLyS discovered
history.detail: Human Genome Sciences scientists identify BLyS from genomic sequencing.

history.title: BLISS trials
history.detail: BLISS-52 and BLISS-76 meet their primary endpoints in SLE.

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in March (US) and July (EU), the first new SLE drug since the 1950s.

history.title: Children
history.detail: IV belimumab approved for children with SLE aged 5 years and older.

history.title: Lupus nephritis
history.detail: Approved for lupus nephritis (BLISS-LN), the first drug approved for this indication.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Belimumab was the first drug approved for lupus since hydroxychloroquine and corticosteroids in the 1950s.
BLyS was among the first drug targets identified directly from genomic sequencing data.
